chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Whoever hurries in the two days, let him not depart until the sun sets; and if evening overtakes him, he stays overnight and does not depart."

key_terms.يَوْمَيْنِ: two days (referring to the 11th and 12th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who leaves Mina before sunset on the days of Tashriq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific legal boundaries for early departure from Mina during the days of Tashriq, emphasizing that 'hurrying' is defined by leaving before the sun reaches its zenith (Zawal). It establishes a practical safeguard for pilgrims, ensuring that those who inadvertently miss the optimal time for departure must remain in Mina until evening, thereby preserving the ritual integrity of the stoning of the Jamarat. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ease with precision in Hajj rituals, as codified by Shaykh al-Tusi.
